find: Snell’s law gives the quantitative relationship between the angles of incidence and refraction: \(n_1 \sin \theta_1 = n_2 \sin \theta_2\), where \(n\) is the refractive index of each medium and \(\theta\) is the angle measured from the normal. For light travelling from air (\(n \approx 1\)) into glass (\(n \approx 1.5\)), the refracted ray is bent towards the normal.
replace: There is no refraction equation on this course, so you never need a refractive index. You do need total internal reflection. When light travels from glass into air, it bends away from the normal. As the angle of incidence inside the glass is made larger, the refracted ray bends further and further until, at the critical angle, it travels along the boundary itself. Above the critical angle no light escapes at all — every ray is reflected back inside the glass. This is how optical fibres carry light around bends.
note: F18: Snell's law and refractive index are nowhere in this spec; replaced with 5.1P total internal reflection and critical angle, which is both-tier and was missing
